correctness.rationale: Using D(n)/n=sum_{p|n} e_p/p, prime powers imply a=p-1. For p<q, a q+b p=(p-1)(q-1), equivalent (a+1)q+(b+1)p=pq+1. For p=2, parity forces a+1 odd>=3 and hence (a+1)q>2q+1 impossible. For odd p, B=b+1>=2 forces 2<=A=a+1<=p-1, uniquely A=q^{-1}(mod p), so q not congruent1 mod p. Conversely for odd p<q with q not congruent1, u inverse in 2..p-1 and k=(u q-1)/p with 1<=k<q; B=q-k cannot equal1 since q(p-u)=p-1 impossible. Thus a=u-1,b=q-1-k uniquely positive. Squarefree a=b=1 forces (p-2)(q-2)=3, giving n=15. Fixed odd p the p-2 allowable nonzero residue classes give asymptotic (p-2)/(p-1)Li(Q) by PNT in AP. Independently enumerated all 2<=p<q<100 primes and positive a<p,b<q; 249 admissible prime supports matched exactly, only squarefree (3,5). The unbounded claim rests on modular proof and PNT in AP.
